clue.text: Drifters not mountain climbing around North Korea's capital

indicators.note: around means the reversed letters are wrapped about the next pieces
in a down clue climbing means the words not and mountain are read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: taken as written
an alp is a mountain
N is the compass abbreviation for north

indicators.note: capital here means the head, the first letter, of the word Korea

explanation.surface: Someone declines to climb a mountain near Pyongyang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'North Korea's capital' suggests Pyongyang, but it splits into North and the first letter of Korea.
explanation.definitionFit: Plankton are tiny organisms that drift with ocean currents rather than swim.

clue.text: King wearing obscure jumper

indicators.note: the obscure word wears the king, holding him inside like clothing

parts.note: to fog is to obscure or cloud
R is the abbreviation for king (Rex)

explanation.surface: A monarch dressed in a drab, dingy sweater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumper' looks like a sweater (British for a pullover), but here it is an animal that jumps.
explanation.definitionFit: A frog is an amphibian famed for leaping, so it is a jumper.

clue.text: Copy key to open bolt

indicators.note: the key goes at the opening, the start, of the word

parts.note: Esc is a key at the top left of a computer keyboard
to ape is to copy or mimic

explanation.surface: Instructions for having a key cut so a lock bolt can be opened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bolt' looks like part of a lock, but it is the verb meaning to run away.
explanation.definitionFit: To bolt is to flee suddenly, and an escape is a getaway.

clue.text: Singer's first disc rising to second place — official!

indicators.note: in a down clue the letter climbs up one slot to become the second letter

parts.note: a crooner is a singer of sentimental songs
O looks like a disc; first picks the first of the two Os

explanation.surface: A singer's debut record climbs to number two in the charts, officially.
explanation.walkthrough: The first O of CROONER moves up one place in the column, giving C-O-R-O-N-E-R.
explanation.definitionFit: A coroner is a public official who investigates sudden or suspicious deaths.

clue.text: Perhaps Rupert Pupkin's on the air, somehow

definitions.note: an example of the answer, hence perhaps

indicators.note: somehow means the letters are arranged in some other way

explanation.surface: A comic character is being broadcast in some fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: Rupert Pupkin is Robert De Niro's would-be comedian in the film The King of Comedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Pupkin is a deluded, unheroic protagonist, a classic example of a central character lacking heroic qualities.

clue.text: 90% discount on opening of neighbourhood business — approach succeeded — they make some noise

indicators.note: the first letter is a Roman numeral, L for 50; cut its value by 90% and it becomes 5, V

parts.note: local means of the neighbourhood
CO is the abbreviation for company, a business
RD is road, an approach to a place
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in family trees

explanation.surface: A shop advertises a huge discount, a sales pitch that worked, attracting a noisy crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: L is 50 in Roman numerals; take 90% off and you have 5, V, so LOCAL becomes VOCAL.
explanation.definitionFit: The vocal cords are the folds in the larynx that vibrate to produce the voice.

clue.text: Songs of praise revealed second thoughts over charity

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over, above, the second

parts.note: a PS, postscript, adds second thoughts to a letter
alms are charitable gifts

explanation.surface: A hymn session shows people having doubts about a charity.
explanation.definitionFit: Psalms are the sacred hymns of the Book of Psalms, sung in worship.

clue.text: Outside broadcast for scale

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: An outside broadcast set up for a large-scale event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outside broadcast' reads as a TV term, but 'Outside' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Al fresco, from Italian, means in the open air, so outdoors.

clue.text: In retrospect, young man's fine cutting corners

indicators.note: fine cuts into the reversed word, splitting it
looking back means the word for young man is read backwards

parts.note: a son is a young man
OK means fine

explanation.surface: A lad looks back and admits it was fine to cut corners.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'has', a link, not a possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Nooks are small recesses or corners of a room.

clue.text: Bar room finally has cordon bleu cooking

indicators.note: finally picks the final letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A pub's back room now offers fine French cuisine.
explanation.walkthrough: A snug is a small, cosy private room in a British pub.
explanation.definitionFit: In British pubs the snug is a small separate room of the bar.

clue.text: A binman, on working with a womble, describes small mythical creature

indicators.note: to describe a circle is to draw round it, so the anagram goes round the next piece
working means the letters are worked into a new shape

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothes labels

explanation.surface: A bin collector teams up with a Womble, the litter-picking TV character, to portray a Yeti.
explanation.walkthrough: The Wombles are furry creatures from a British children's series who tidy up rubbish, so they fit with a binman.
explanation.definitionFit: The Yeti is a legendary ape-like beast said to roam the Himalayas.

clue.text: On the counter, say with peppers filling dish

indicators.note: counter means going against, so the words say and peppers are read backwards

parts.note: EG, for example, is what say means
to pepper is to dot or sprinkle

explanation.surface: A cook puts stuffed peppers on the kitchen counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'filling' looks like stuffing for peppers, but 'filling dish' is the definition: stodge is heavy food.
explanation.definitionFit: Stodge is heavy, starchy food that fills you up, like suet pudding.

clue.text: Investing own money in bad film is common

indicators.note: investing one thing in another puts it inside

parts.note: dark can mean evil or bad
ET is Spielberg's film E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial

explanation.surface: Someone puts their own cash into a flop of a movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad film' reads as one phrase, but bad gives DARK and the film is E.T., Spielberg's alien hit.
explanation.definitionFit: Downmarket means cheap and lowbrow, so vulgar or common.

clue.text: Queen's duty-bound to practice

indicators.note: the duty surrounds the queen, binding her inside

parts.note: excise is a duty or tax on goods
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: The monarch is obliged to rehearse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'practice' is used as a verb (British spelling is practise); 'to' marks it as one.
explanation.definitionFit: To exercise is to train or drill, as practising a skill does.

clue.text: See 11
Uncover fatty bits with topless, risqué pose

indicators.note: uncovering strips off the outside letters of each word
topless means the top, first, letter in this down clue is removed

parts.note: rude means risqué or smutty

explanation.surface: A saucy instruction to strip off for a revealing photo pose.
explanation.walkthrough: Strip FATTY and BITS to ATT and IT, and take the R off RUDE.
explanation.definitionFit: An attitude is a posture of the body, a stance struck for effect.

clue.text: 4 down, 1 to go — lay waste

indicators.note: to go means the number is removed

parts.note: the answer to 4 down
1 is one
a lay is a poem or song, an ode

explanation.surface: A coroner's grim list: one case left before the land is laid waste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lay waste' reads as one phrase, but lay is ODE and only 'waste' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: To corrode is to eat away gradually, so to waste something.

clue.text: Military Intelligence inside give command

indicators.note: inside means the first piece goes within the second

parts.note: to donate is to give

explanation.surface: Army intelligence officers on the inside issue an order.
explanation.definitionFit: To dominate is to control or hold sway over, to have command of.

clue.text: Guide for audience to put on face mask

indicators.note: for an audience means as heard, by sound

parts.note: to add is to put on; a visor shields the face

explanation.surface: Stage directions telling a performer to don a mask for the crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: An advisor counsels and steers others, a guide.

clue.text: Expert politician, Kennedy could be motivated

parts.note: a pro is an expert
MP is a Member of Parliament
Ted Kennedy, the US senator

explanation.surface: A skilled politician named Kennedy might be driven.
explanation.definitionFit: Prompted means moved to act, spurred or motivated.

clue.text: Weather is interrupting break

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking into the middle of the next word

parts.note: a rest is a break

explanation.surface: Bad weather is spoiling a holiday break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weather' looks like rain, but it is the verb, as in weather a storm.
explanation.definitionFit: To weather a crisis is to withstand or resist it.

clue.text: Oil producer's assets essentially unchanged

indicators.note: essentially means the essence, the middle letters, of assets

parts.note: same means unchanged

explanation.surface: An oil company's assets remain basically the same.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oil producer' suggests a petroleum firm, but it is a plant whose seeds give oil.
explanation.definitionFit: Sesame seeds are pressed for sesame oil, used in cooking.

clue.text: Bundles that man and a female on board ship

indicators.note: on board means inside the ship

parts.note: SS is steamship
he is that man

explanation.surface: Packages for a man and a woman on a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheafs are bundles of things such as papers or harvested corn.

clue.text: Weirdly, I censor intern after dismissing the news desk

indicators.note: weirdly means strangely arranged
after dismissing means some letters are removed before rearranging

parts.note: read as the N's: all three Ns

explanation.surface: A newsroom censor deals oddly with a junior, after firing the news desk team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'news desk' reads as a newspaper office, but 'the news' is read as the Ns, all three letters N.
explanation.definitionFit: An escritoire is a writing desk with drawers and a hinged writing surface.

clue.text: Ages in Westgate-on-Sea

indicators.note: in means the letters lie inside the place name

explanation.surface: Time seems endless in a seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: Westgate-on-Sea is a seaside resort in Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: Eons are vast spans of time, ages.

clue.text: All wanting a ring to copy

indicators.note: wanting means lacking the letter a

parts.note: each means all, as in a pound each
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: Everyone wants a wedding ring to imitate.
explanation.definitionFit: An echo repeats a sound, so it is an imitation or copy.

clue.text: Pass leads to simple poacher's goal

indicators.note: leads are the first letters of each word

parts.note: an end is a goal or aim

explanation.surface: A football pass that sets up an easy tap-in for a goal poacher.
explanation.walkthrough: A poacher is a footballer who scores scrappy goals; here pass means pass time.
explanation.definitionFit: To spend time is to pass it.

clue.text: First to move on from Cream?

indicators.note: on means the second piece comes next, after the first

parts.note: off can mean from, as in off the shelf
in chess, White moves first

explanation.surface: Someone is the first member to quit the band Cream.
explanation.walkthrough: Cream were a 1960s rock band; the question mark shows cream is an example of the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Cream is a pale yellowish shade, an example of a colour close to white.
